title: The AI Ledger
introduction: Reviewed through November 17 at 20:00 UTC. GPT-6.2 leads a busy model and harness day, alongside Microsoft coding models in Copilot, Entra sign-in preview and review controls. Late November 16 releases retain their actual dates. Yesterday’s snapshot is archived unchanged. The two-publisher controls forecast is now met by Claude Code and Copilot CLI; remaining forecasts retain their original criteria. No fresh timing rumor met the evidence threshold. Confidence is qualitative, not a probability.

items.title: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch with lower Astra API rates
items.summary: OpenAI releases Astra for demanding projects and Sol for everyday work in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API. Standard Astra input/output rates fall 20% versus GPT-6 Astra; Sol retains GPT-6.1 Sol pricing. Efficiency and quality improvements remain publisher claims.
items.whyItMatters: Pro $200 gains Ultrafast for Sol; Pro $500 supports either model. Work and Codex share usage. API Ultrafast availability is separate from subscription entitlements. OpenAI also warns that tighter cyber safeguards can restrict legitimate security research.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: This is a confirmed November 17 launch, not the earlier documentation sightings. The model release is distinct from Codex CLI prereleases. No benchmark claim here establishes superiority on a particular repository.

items.title: MAI Code 2 and Flash arrive in Copilot
items.summary: GitHub adds MAI Code 2 for complex agentic coding and MAI Code 2 Flash for lighter everyday tasks. Both appear in supported clients including Copilot CLI; billing is usage-based. Flash includes Free and Student eligibility, while Code 2 starts with paid Copilot plans.
items.whyItMatters: These provide additional candidates for coding evaluations within Copilot. Business and Enterprise model policies govern access; advertised availability does not prove a given organization has enabled them.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: These are Microsoft model additions announced at Ignite, not a rename of GPT or Claude and not an announcement of unrestricted local weights.

items.title: Copilot CLI previews Entra sign-in, but not on Linux yet
items.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.113 or later supports Microsoft Entra authentication in public preview on Windows and macOS. Linked OIDC Enterprise Managed Users require assigned Copilot Business or Enterprise access and CLI policy enablement. A separate eligible Microsoft 365 Copilot route uses Microsoft 365 inference and does not require a GitHub account.
items.whyItMatters: The two entitlement paths have different billing and model policies. Linux support is promised later, so this is not yet a Linux-VPS sign-in solution. Separately, 1.0.113 lets administrators disable built-in Browser Use even in running sessions.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: This is authentication and administration functionality, not automatic entitlement for every Entra tenant or Microsoft 365 account.

items.title: Copilot review adds adaptive effort and secret detection previews
items.summary: Adaptive chooses Lite, Balanced or Max within configured limits; Balanced remains the default. Cross-repository context is previewed for public repositories, and secret detection combines deterministic detectors with AI. Copilot review for Azure Repos becomes generally available.
items.whyItMatters: Review depth can respond to risk without exceeding the administrator’s cap. Secret findings still need human investigation; these features do not guarantee a clean repository. Azure Repos support is not GitLab support.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: The announcement mixes public previews with a separate Azure Repos GA release. Do not present every component as generally available.

items.title: Added Nov 17: Copilot retires three older model options
items.summary: The November 16 retirement notice covers Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Terra across most Copilot experiences. Exceptions: Opus 4.8 remains for individual annual subscribers, and Opus 5 retains authorized runtime refusal fallback despite leaving the picker.
items.whyItMatters: Check pinned model choices. GitHub suggests Opus 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol/GPT-6 Luna, subject to enterprise policy; do not assume a newly launched model is automatically enabled.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: These retirements were announced October 15 and took effect November 16. This issue adds the missed dated notice retrospectively, not as a November 17 retirement.

items.title: Late Nov 16: Claude Code hardens background sessions and prompts
items.summary: Version 2.1.326 supports Code Mode with agent teams. It fixes unintended acceptance at trust and auto-mode prompts, warns when permission settings cannot be saved, and stops background sessions before model calls if their inherited gateway configuration is lost.
items.whyItMatters: Relevant regression tests include accidental Enter presses, failed settings writes and crash recovery. These are publisher-reported fixes, not proof of universal safety.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: Published at 22:11 UTC after the previous 20:00 cutoff. It is a harness release, not a new Claude model.

items.title: Qwen Code 0.28 unifies loops and adds Qwen4-Max controls
items.summary: Headless sessions, the terminal UI and subagents use the shared agent loop by default. The release adds Qwen4-Max effort, cache TTL and image-detail support, preserves the latest complete operation during compaction, and enables external workspace execution.
items.whyItMatters: More consistent runtime paths may simplify orchestration, but permission boundaries and interruption recovery still require workload-specific tests.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: This follows the November 15 stable 0.27.4 release. The separately numbered 1.0 preview channel should not be confused with this stable release.

items.title: Late Nov 16: Hermes ships a stable rollup with durable subagents
items.summary: Hermes 0.23.2 lists subagents that survive gateway restarts or crashes and can continue in their own conversations. The publisher defers full curated notes to 0.24.0; immediate fixes include duplicate recovery replies and incomplete reconnect rendering.
items.whyItMatters: Persistence claims are useful for long-running workflows, but validate recovery before depending on it. The installer-based Desktop bundle does not update with this release; the publisher distinguishes that from CLI, Store and container delivery.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: Published 20:59 UTC, after yesterday’s cutoff. A large patch-version rollup does not mean every listed feature was introduced on that date.

items.title: OpenCode 1 patch offers migration and trims oversized image history
items.summary: OpenCode 1.19.6 offers a user-controlled upgrade to OpenCode 2, preserving sessions, projects and settings; version-1 plugins need updates. Above 25 MiB of image history, older images become placeholders. Oversized-body provider errors trigger compaction and retry.
items.whyItMatters: This recovers requests by removing older image content, not by losslessly compressing it. Re-check whether required visual evidence remains available.
items.confidenceReason: Official sources establish the dated release and reported behavior; no independent performance test was run.
items.historicalContext: This is maintenance of the OpenCode 1 line, not a downgrade from the OpenCode 2.3 release covered last week.

items.title: Qwen4-Max launches beyond the separate preview
items.summary: QwenCloud lists qwen4-max for multimodal reasoning, coding and agent tasks, with tool calling, structured outputs, explicit caching and reasoning summaries. The specifications list a one-million-token context window and pay-as-you-go access.
items.whyItMatters: A new hosted candidate for long-context agent evaluations. Test compatibility and costs on your workload; this is not evidence of local weight availability or benchmark superiority.
items.confidenceReason: Official publisher sources support the announcement. Capabilities have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: The November 11 qwen4-max-preview was a distinct Token Plan preview. Today’s dated entry uses qwen4-max; do not count the preview and launch as two unrelated model families.

items.title: OpenAI adds a specialized image-safety classifier
items.summary: Approved organizations can use omni-moderation-csam-latest through the moderation API without charge. It supplies distinct signals for possible child sexual abuse material and possible AI-generated CSAM to prioritize human review.
items.whyItMatters: Relevant to eligible trust-and-safety teams, not a coding-model upgrade. A classifier signal is not a definitive judgment and does not replace review.
items.confidenceReason: Official publisher sources support the announcement. Capabilities have not been independently tested for this newsletter.
items.historicalContext: This is a specialized moderation release, separate from OpenAI’s general-purpose GPT and coding models.

items.whyItMatters: Do not treat an alpha artifact as a stable rollout or infer new model support from the version number. Existing stable users need not switch solely because an alpha exists.

items.title: Resolved Nov 17 · two-harness controls forecast: met
items.summary: We expect at least two of Codex, Claude Code, Copilot CLI and OpenCode to publish stable releases that add or fix permission, background-task or session-control behavior during the next calendar week.
items.whyItMatters: Cross-publisher progress would be stronger evidence of an operational-controls trend than another isolated patch.
items.confidenceReason: Recent releases support the direction, but the count and timing are editorial forecasts, not publisher commitments or calculated probabilities. Resolution: stable Claude Code 2.1.326 (November 16) fixes permission and background-session behavior; stable Copilot CLI 1.0.113 (November 17) adds administrator control of Browser Use during running sessions. These two distinct publishers satisfy the original criterion.
items.historicalContext: The November 9 and November 10 follow-up forecasts each required only one release and were met. This prospectively raises the threshold to two distinct harnesses and excludes the current week.

items.resolutionCriteria: Pass if official stable releases from at least two distinct named harnesses have published_at dates from November 16 through November 22 and explicitly document a permission, background-task or session-control addition or fix. Count each harness once. Prereleases, documentation-only changes and model support alone do not count. Otherwise fail at 23:59 UTC November 22.
items.counterarguments: Recent patches may reduce immediate demand, releases may cluster before the window, or work may stay in prerelease.
